newsitem.title: UK: Billiton says priorities expansion, privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Billiton says priorities expansion, privatisation.

text.p: Billiton, the South African non-precious mining house which is planning to list on London's stock exchange, said on Monday its priorities for growth lay in expanding existing operations and taking advantage of privatisations in emerging markets.

Chairman and chief executive Brian Gilbertson said the decision to seek its main listing in London as part of a demerger from South Africa's Gencor Ltd was to allow Billiton to "compete for shareholder value on an equal footing with other mining groups" for the first time.
"We need to access international capital to continue (our) record of growth," Gilbertson told a news conference to launch the group's flotation prospectus.
"South Africa's foreign exchange controls have proved a significant handicap to our ambitions," he added.
The company said it was "very confident" that it would be allowed to join Britain's FTSE index of 100 leading companies later this year.
Billiton, which has established its international headquarters in London, will issue around 375 million shares priced at between 210 and 240 pence, with dealing expected to start on July 23.
If the guide price is achieved, the resulting market capitalisation of between 4.4 and 5.1 billion stg would put it comfortably in the middle of the UK's leading shares index.
The company said it expected non-South African shareholders to hold between 25 and 30 percent of the company after the share issue, with British institutions taking the lead.
Gilbertson said increased financial muscle would allow Billiton to take advantage of opportunities around the world as they arose.
"The balance sheet is robust, with substantial debt capacity," Gilbertson said.
Among existing operations, he said the focus was on process improvements at the group's aluminium plant at Worsley in Australia and an expansion of capacity of nickel mining operations in Colombia.
The Alumar operation in northern Brazil would be expanded "when the time is right," Gilbertson said.
Plans to develop an aluminium smelter in Mozambique, announced on June 24, would lead to an investment by Billiton of around $125 million if it went ahead.

Billiton said it was also examining setting up a zinc smelter in South Africa and looking at the feasibility of a new nickel operation at a site in western Australia, where Gilbertson said "the nickel grades are the highest ever seen in Australia."
Billiton outlined a number of potential targets in mining and process operations currently slated for privatisation, notably in Venezuela, Colombia and Brazil.
"Our track record leaves us well placed to benefit from these opportunities," Gilbertson said.
Aluminium provides the biggest chunk of Billiton's attributable profits, which are expected to be at least $330 million in the year ended June 30,1997.
"I would like to see the percentage of aluminium shrink a little, but only through growth in other divisions," Gilbertson told reporters.
